function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is a formal authorization or instruction that gives a person or entity (the *mandator*) the power to act on behalf of another (the *mandatee*). In practice it’s a contract‑like agreement that specifies what actions the mandatary may perform, under what conditions, and for how long. Key points: | Aspect | Typical meaning | |--------|-----------------| | **Legal/Contractual basis** | A written or verbal agreement that defines the scope of authority. | | **Common contexts** | • Banking & finance – e.g., standing orders, direct debits, investment instructions.
• Corporate governance – board resolutions authorizing officers to sign contracts.
• Government – delegating powers to agencies or officials. | | **Typical content** | • Parties involved
• Scope of authority (what can be done)
• Duration / termination conditions
• Any limits or conditions (e.g., maximum amounts, reporting requirements) | | **Statuses** | • **Active** – currently valid and enforceable.
• **Pending** – awaiting approval or activation.
• **Inactive** – expired, revoked, or cancelled. | In many systems you’ll see APIs that let you query mandates by status (active, pending, inactive) or by the name of the client whose mandates you’re interested in.
